text.text: If only there were six stars to give! The service was really attentive. We ordered beef and duck breast for the main course, both options were fantastic. The food amount was fulfilling and the taste was great. For the appetizer, I strongly recommend the refreshing seasonal fish. The soft-shell crab was not as impressing. However, all other dishes were great. The space between each table was comfortable. We love the overall experience!

text.text:
All the dishes were quite delicious, just the portion is not very big to begin with so may have to order more if you’re with a group! We basically ordered everything on the menu. The desert tiramisu was yummy, with a hint of peanut?
They didn’t have the lasagna so be sure to ask when you call because not all the items will be available!

Just a bit disappointed that for a bistro, they are charging water and there was no tap water option. If you’re hoping for coffee, tea, there won’t be but there’s a wide selection of alcohol. We thought going for brunch might mean other beverage selections, have to check more carefully next time.

It’s downstairs so if it’s sunny day, you might feel like you’re missing out on the sun but the decor and environment is cozy!

text.text: This spot is such a hidden gem! The basement dining area is modern, well-lit, and has a cozy feel. My menu choices were beautifully presented and tasted just as good. We’re looking forward to coming back on a weekend when it’s a bit livelier to soak more of the atmosphere!

text.text: Comfy and relaxed were the first impressions when we arrived this basement dining hall.  It wasn’t like what I was expected (filled with young crowds and noisy), instead it was quiet and peaceful.  Initially we were greeted by a young maitre d'  who seemed concerning about our wish to dine in this restaurant and kindly offered us to checkout the menu before leading us to the basement (the dining hall); where was beautifully decorated ( be mindful your head as the staircase’s ceiling was a bit low for taller people), the seating area was carefully divided for different groups of guests.  We couldn’t figure out the region of dishes, perhaps it’s a fusion style as the menu covers around the world.  The price is a little dear, fine dining range, but the table setting was a bit like steakhouse （clothe serviette wrapped cutleries).  We order two set menus with the duck and fish. Duck was thick, beautifully presented (needed a little more flavour), the fish was superb, freshly prepared, matched well with the French green sauce. Good selection of wine for our main. Dessert were Tiramisu and Crème Brûlée; very safe choice. I’m looking forward to seeing if the team would take a challenge to offer higher skilled of desserts as a highlight of ending the dining experience. Overall, it was a pleasant experience and very full belly.:)
